s1.syndrome_frame: Rapidly progressive visual impairment with endocrine dysfunction
salient_findings: Sellar/suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm
key_facts: 2-week history of rapidly progressive visual reduction
Vestibular schwannoma treated by gamma-knife radiosurgery 2 years earlier
Sellar/suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm
Lesion predominantly isointense to gray matter on T1-weighted images
Diffuse homogeneous enhancement after contrast administration
Normal pituitary gland on MRI 2 years earlier

shortlist.label: Pituitary adenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Sellar/suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm, abnormal thyroid-stimulating hormone level, and elevated prolactin level

shortlist.label: Craniopharyngioma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly progressive visual reduction, sellar/suprasellar mass, and endocrine dysfunction

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Sellar/suprasellar mass, abnormal thyroid-stimulating hormone level, and rapidly progressive visual impairment

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Sellar/suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm and diffuse homogeneous enhancement after contrast administration

shortlist.label: Pituitary apoplexy
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly progressive visual reduction, sellar/suprasellar mass, and abnormal endocrine function

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with rapidly progressive visual reduction, bitemporal hemianopsia, and a sellar/suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm, along with abnormal endocrine levels and an elevated prolactin level, is most consistent with a pituitary adenoma.

rejected.label: Craniopharyngioma
rejected.why: Typically presents in childhood or adolescence and often has calcifications on imaging, which were not mentioned.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Would be less likely to cause such specific endocrine abnormalities and bitemporal hemianopsia without other systemic symptoms.

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: Usually has a dural tail on imaging and is less commonly associated with endocrine dysfunction.

rejected.label: Pituitary apoplexy
rejected.why: Typically presents with sudden, severe headache and visual loss, often with acute hormonal deficiencies, which does not fully match the patient's gradual onset of symptoms.
